observations.behavior: Adds story response data and helper functions for an Insights page tab.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides mock trend responses including the new 'Issues created' chart. No backend or shared-query implementation is shown; this could support UI development but does not establish a working feature.

observations.behavior: Renders a ChartCard component with title "Issues created" using issuesCreatedQuery.
observations.posthog_connection: Connects to the Error Tracking insights view. This demonstrates frontend wiring only; no change to HogQL, warehouse ingestion, or event processing is visible.

observations.behavior: Defines buildIssuesCreatedQuery returning an InsightVizNode with HogQL math_hogql: uniqIf(issue_id, timestamp = issue_first_seen).
observations.posthog_connection: Adds HogQL query construction for counting unique issues by first-seen exception. This could enable a metric without changing PostHog's core ingestion or storage behavior.

observations.limitations: All hunks are confined to TypeScript frontend and Rust tests. There is no modification of hogql/, warehouse connectors, managed warehouse, person identity replication, CSP middleware, migrations, or shared schema that would demonstrate systemic benefit or production readiness. The tier cannot be raised because there is no evidence of broader capability or risk reduction across components.

review.reason: Changes are narrow and localized: adding a new chart and its supporting query builder and story mocks in the Error Tracking Insights tab. No backend implementation, migration, or cross-component dependency changes are shown. This does not meet criteria for tier 3 (broader capability) nor tier 2 (substantive bounded improvement demonstrated end-to-end).
review.posthog_relevance: Could support development of an "Issues created" insight view; relevance depends on whether this becomes part of shipped functionality. Without backend or shared-query changes, it remains a UI-only addition.
review.uncertainty: The chunk omits any backend, database, or shared-schema implementation. It also lacks release notes or adoption indicators. Tier assignment relies solely on visible code, which points to a small, self-contained change.
